trials.notes: Used the correct WP_HTML_Processor fragment parser, documented token walking APIs, get_attribute(), get_modifiable_text(), get_token_type(), get_tag(), and is_tag_closer(). The single-pass active-link stack is consistent with the docs' repeated-region guidance and handled decoded text, decoded href, valueless href, and unclosed input. Minor reservation: it implements its own anchor stack instead of the simpler documented depth-bounded subtree pattern.

Used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), next_tag(), get_current_depth(), next_token(), get_token_type(), get_modifiable_text(), and get_attribute() exactly along documented patterns. It correctly filtered href with is_string(), preserving null/true/empty-string semantics, and used decoded API values rather than re-decoding.

Same documented HTML Processor approach as trial-2. The class_exists() guard is a PHP builtin, not hallucinated HTML API usage. All HTML API methods used are present in the rendered docs and execution reported no _doing_it_wrong misuse.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: all three passed simple, no-href-excluded, entity-in-href-decoded, valueless-href, image-link-empty-text, entities-in-text, no-links, and unclosed-link. The docs worked well in four places: the HTML Processor overview says to choose it for structure, subtree walking, and text collection; get_attribute() exposes string|true|null so models filtered with is_string(); get_modifiable_text() says ordinary DOM-style text requires get_token_type() === '#text' and is already decoded; next_token()/get_current_depth() explain depth-bounded walks, >= guards, and virtual closers for malformed or incomplete input. Near-miss: the next_token() warning against nested loops sits close to a subtree-text recipe that uses an inner bounded loop. The successful candidates interpreted that correctly, but the distinction could be sharper.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor method section shows string|true|null and boolean/null examples, but the decoded-string contract and empty-string-vs-valueless distinction are clearer in the Tag Processor docs than here.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Mirror the inherited attribute-value contract directly in the HTML Processor docs: absent returns null, valueless returns true, present empty value returns '', and string values are already character-reference decoded.

doc_gaps.problem: The warning not to nest next_token() loops can read as forbidding the common next_tag()+depth-bounded subtree scan pattern used for repeated elements.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short contrast between unsafe nested cursor walks and safe depth-bounded subtree scans that intentionally consume the current element before resuming the outer search.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs have a single-element text recipe, but less explicit guidance for collecting text from every matching element in document order while also reading attributes from each opener.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general repeated-element extraction recipe, not link-specific, showing: match an opener, read/filter attributes, record opener depth, append only descendant #text tokens, then continue scanning.
